correctness.rationale: The graph vertices, edges, intrinsic metric and the Čech facet formula are explicitly defined; a complete face-enumeration test gives 211 scale-2 faces and 1,279 scale-3 faces. A standalone verified 626-pair free-face list collapses all and only the 1,252 scale-3 faces outside the 27-face octahedral sphere. At scale two, two complete acyclic discrete-Morse matchings each have 98 pairs and critical cells one vertex plus 13 two-cells; the script exhaustively tests 578 oriented incidences, and independent mod-two ranks agree. These furnish integral homotopy equivalences; inclusions give split-surjective H2 with rank-12 kernel. All 48 group symmetries are checked on graph edges and the octahedral oriented cycle. Limits: no other scales, no equivariant collapse, no independently conducted audit.

originality.rationale: Final claim-to-theorem comparisons found no covering published statement. The exact scale-three octahedral elementary collapse and the primitive scale-two-to-three integral persistence map concern the fourteen-vertex radial incidence graph of the cube, rather than the regular hypercube, twelve-vertex cuboctahedral line graph, or vertex-truncation family treated in the closest publications. The 2014 even-scale distance-neighborhood thesis and 2025 general closed-neighborhood equivalences also do not supply this graph-specific collapse. This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness theorem.
residual_risks: An unpublished, inaccessible or differently indexed exact calculation for the Fruchard/Miquel/radial-cube graph might exist.
The 2014 thesis and 2025 translations were compared on relevant source material; not every result in the global closed-neighborhood literature is searchable.
Symmetry is only on the integral H2 module, not an equivariant collapse; no broader equivariant homotopy equivalence is claimed.

value.rationale: The rhombic dodecahedron is the natural 14-vertex vertex–face radial graph of a cube. Its six high-degree vertices canonically form the octahedral surface subcomplex, which surprisingly controls a pure 6-dimensional Čech nerve via 626 explicit elementary collapses. The scale-two 13-sphere wedge and the primitive integral 2-to-3 persistence map explain precisely which second-dimensional class remains: the geometric octahedral fundamental cycle. The determinant character links topology with the complete 48-element polyhedral symmetry group. This is a motivated, exact structural finite classification beyond textbook deductions or a random graph census; no general radial-graph theorem or persistence in unexamined degrees is claimed.
